A.summary: Your responses indicate mild joint strain or early wear with a low indication for surgical intervention. Conservative management, guided physiotherapy, and targeted exercise are typically recommended.
possible_causes: Mild muscle strain or patellofemoral tracking stress
Early non-structural joint inflammation or overuse
A.next_step: Maintain active joint strengthening and monitor your symptoms. If pain increases during activities, schedule an OPD evaluation.

B.summary: Your responses indicate moderate knee joint symptoms that warrant formal clinical and diagnostic evaluation. Further radiological assessment (X-ray or MRI) will clarify joint space and soft tissue health.
possible_causes: Moderate cartilage wear or early osteoarthritis
B.next_step: A specialized clinical examination and diagnostic imaging review with Dr. Pulak Vatsya is recommended to prevent progressive joint damage.

C.summary: Your responses indicate significant joint impairment and high symptom severity. A comprehensive orthopaedic evaluation is strongly recommended to explore joint preservation or surgical treatment pathways.
possible_causes: Advanced knee osteoarthritis / severe cartilage breakdown
Significant structural ligament damage or chronic joint instability
C.next_step: Schedule a priority consultation with Dr. Pulak Vatsya to review MRI/X-ray scans and discuss non-surgical and advanced surgical options.

R.summary: CRITICAL MEDICAL SAFETY ALERT: Your reported symptoms include acute red-flag criteria (such as mechanical joint locking, inability to bear weight, or joint swelling accompanied by fever).
possible_causes: Acute mechanical joint blockage or displaced meniscal bucket-handle tear
Possible acute septic arthritis, severe trauma, or major ligament rupture
R.next_step: Immediate clinical evaluation at an orthopaedic clinic or emergency facility is required. Do not force movement on a locked or non-weight-bearing knee.
